notes: Corrected: the *it* of *it is good* is the anticipatory subject of an extraposed infinitive clause the Hebrew writes (`זַמְּרָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ`), so rule 25's extraposition sentence makes it `added` and leaves *is good* on `טוֹב`. The third colon is left as accepted, because there the ASV coordinates `נָאוָה תְהִלָּה` as its own clause and extraposes nothing, so rule 20's construction-supplied *it is* stands with `נָעִים`.
The alternative rendering in the margin (*Or, For he is good ... For he is gracious*) was read and set aside; the printed text governs, by rule 38.
